message.text: The gate never takes a round's own status. Each counted round adds its findings to the merge, and a round of the exact merge diff adds to `covered` every check it ran. That holds even when the round itself reads not reviewed because another check failed. The gate passes once the union of checks that ran in *some* round covers the tier. A check that failed in one round is hidden by a run of that check that passed in another. The base decides this the other way: "The gate takes the worst standing round ... not reviewed is worse than blocking", and the gate "computes the verdict of each standing round ... and exits with the worst". The round-replaces-none ruling chose to write empty `replaces` lists so that a later passing round could not hide an earlier round's failed check before #395 decided who may replace what.

evidence.snippet: | `melian gate <#pr>` | Decides whether the pull request's head may merge into its base tip now, from the shared records on `melian/state` alone, under the base tip's policy, and writes nothing. It counts every round of the head whose base the base tip holds, takes each one's findings under the base tip's policy, and counts a check as covered only by a round of exactly the merge base to the head that stands as reviewed. It reads nothing unless the base tip's root `melian.yaml` sets `trust.writers: true`. On standard error it names each counted round and what it covers, or why it covers nothing, each reason it cannot decide, and each finding a later round made live again with the `dismiss` command that clears it, then the command that starts a new round. It prints the merged verdict as `findings` does. A store's failure prints its code, never git's words | `0` may merge, `1` a finding blocks or awaits an answer, `2` the records do not review the merge, or it refused or failed |
- **The gate takes the worst standing round.** Two rounds that stand together, because two hosts reviewed at once, gate by the worse, and not reviewed is worse than blocking.

- The gate is a command, `melian gate "#N"`. It lists the record, computes the verdict of each standing round for the pull request's base and head, and exits with the worst. Any provider's CI can run it. The merge-group check runs it and writes the group's status; a status on the head is a display, and no gate reads one. Just before it writes that status, or copies an override, the check lists again, and computes again when the set differs from the one it read, as [the coordination decision](2026-11-08-how-melian-coordinates.md) requires of any job that writes from an authority it read earlier.
- An unresolved acknowledge finding fails the gate, as a blocking finding does and as [the acknowledge status rule](2026-10-17-acknowledge-status-exact-rule.md) has it for a host's publication. A writer resolves one by recording the read as a dismissal with its reason, from any host, since a dismissal now reaches the record. [The Actions round's status](2026-11-07-actions-round-sets-melian-review.md) exempted an Actions round because a runner could not dismiss; that reason is gone, and so is the exemption once the gate is the required check. The maintainer ruled so on 2026-11-13, in the coordinator's session. Until then the Actions status keeps its own rule, as a display.

Rule 4 has a round name, in `replaces`, the earlier rounds of its revision it replaces, and a round stands when no round that counts names it there. [Issue #395](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/395) has not yet decided who may replace what. The first export wrote every round already in the store at the revision into `replaces`.

Example: host A's round blocks on a failed guardrails check. Host B reviews the same head later and finds nothing. B's round lists A's round in `replaces` though B never read A's records. Today a reader shows every round, so nothing changes. Once [issue #395](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/395) gives `replaces` standing, B's round would hide A's block, and records are immutable, so B's list could never be taken back.

## Choice

- A, as first built: name every round already stored.
- C: name only this writer's own rounds, which needs a writer ID that records do not carry.
- D: name nothing until [issue #395](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/395) decides who may replace what.

The maintainer chose D. Every round's `replaces` list is empty, and `ReviewRecords.round` still takes the list, so [issue #395](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/395) can fill it without a new payload version. A reader shows every round of the revision, ordered by ID.

explanation.whyHere: The change puts a new standard in place of the gate's rule: it keeps the successful run of each check and drops the failed ones. That standard is written only in head text (the new `melian gate` row in docs/guidelines/cli.md and the plan entry), with no decision that supersedes or amends rule 4 or rule 9. Because the selection keeps exactly the records that passed, the sample the gate judges hides the failures the base rule exists to surface.

properties.failureScenario:
Host A runs a round of pull request #N at exactly merge-base..H. Its guardrails check fails (status `failed`), so A's own verdict is not reviewed; this is the round-replaces-none decision's own example. The `melian round` workflow is rerun, as the gate's own message suggests ("To review it again: gh workflow run melian-round.yml"). Round B at the same revision runs everything clean, and both rounds are relayed with empty `replaces`.

In `RecordGate.decide`:
- `coverage()` for A returns every check in `reviewed.ran` except guardrails, since a failed check is not in `ran`.
- `coverage()` for B returns every check.
- `covered` becomes the union, so `gaps` is empty and `failures` is empty.
- `#merged` reads status `passed`, and `melian gate` exits 0.

Under the active base rule the gate takes the worst standing round, which is A's not reviewed, and exits 2. The same holds when A's lens.correctness failed on a provider limit and B's lens.contracts failed on a content filter: neither round alone reviewed the merge, and the gate still passes.

message.text: The gate counts every record in `melian/state` for any pull request (`counts: everyRecordCounts`). Its reason, in the comment, is that only a writer can add there and the base tip trusts writers. It never asks whether the head comes from a fork. Rule 6 of the shared record decision says: "For a fork's head the gate counts only records that key signed, so a repository that has not pinned it passes no fork's pull request, and the gate names what to set up". It says this holds "whatever `trust.writers` says", because a writer's round of a fork's head was made where the fork's code could touch the result.

evidence.snippet:
// A head whose writer Melian cannot establish hands over what a fork's may, which is less.
	const fork = !(await writerTrust(provider, pullRequest)).trusted;

- One that takes pull requests from forks, whatever `trust.writers` says, because without the key the gate cannot tell the trusted host's record of a fork's head from a writer's. For a fork's head the gate counts only records that key signed, so a repository that has not pinned it passes no fork's pull request, and the gate names what to set up. The maintainer ruled so on 2026-11-13, in the coordinator's session, over the alternative of a writer's recorded vouch: the rule's promise is that a fork's head was reviewed where its code could not touch the result, and a vouch promises only that a writer read it.

  This changes one clause of the coverage ledger decision's "Fork heads" section, which said no round of a fork's head records coverage, whoever runs it. A round the trusted host ran and signed now does. That section already named this end: in milestone 3 the agent refuses a record "whose head is not a writer's or the App's", and the trusted host is that App. The rest of the section stands. A writer's round of a fork's head records no coverage and reads not reviewed, with `--trust-head` or without it, because a writer's machine ran the fork's code where it could touch the result. A record of a fork's head with no signature, a bad one, or one from a key the base does not pin covers nothing. A repository with no pinned key passes no fork's pull request.

explanation.whatToDo: In `gate`, call `writerTrust(provider, pullRequest)` as `relay.ts` does. For a head that is not a writer's, refuse with exit 2 and name the signing key that rule 6 needs, until the gate can count signed records. Add a test with a fork's head that a round in melian/state reviewed.
explanation.whyHere: A record of a fork's head is trusted only because of where it sits, the writers' branch, and not because anything checked that the trusted host produced it. No signing key exists yet, so under the base the gate should pass no fork's pull request at all. The head passes one whenever a round of its head is in the store.

properties.failureScenario: Pull request #N comes from a fork (`headRepository` is someone else's). A writer reviews it on their own machine with `melian review "#N" --trust-head --records dir:x`. The fork's tests run there under `--trust-head`. The writer then adds the round's records to `melian/state` directly, which the base decision notes a writer can always do, since `melian records relay` refuses a fork's round. `melian gate "#N"` passes `trustsWriters()` and counts the round with `everyRecordCounts`. If that round covers the tier and found nothing, `RecordGate.decide` reads `passed` and the gate exits 0. Under rule 6 a fork's pull request passes nothing until a pinned key signed its records.

message.text: `#merged` drops every finding whose path is not a file of the merge's diff and that has no trigger on it. It applies that filter to every counted round, including the round of exactly merge-base..H. The filter is there to drop a wider, older-base round's findings in files the merge no longer touches. But a pre-existing finding has no trigger, since a trigger names the hunk that caused it. So every pre-existing finding in a file the change did not touch is dropped from the exact round too. Under a `resolution.preExisting` cap of `acknowledge`, such a finding resolves acknowledge. The acknowledge-status rule says it "then takes the repository-wide acknowledgement gate", and rule 9 says "An unresolved acknowledge finding fails the gate".

## The cap on pre-existing findings

By default a pre-existing finding never resolves above `advisory`. [The decision that holds the verifier's re-scope](2026-10-13-re-scope-held-for-the-compiler.md) lists the important ones under their own heading. This key lets a folder ask for more than a listing.

```yaml
resolution:
  preExisting:
    P0: acknowledge
    P1: acknowledge
```

- Each severity takes `advisory` or `acknowledge`. The default is `advisory` for every severity. `block` is refused.
- The key is a cap, never a requirement. A pre-existing finding resolves to the lesser of its result under the precedence above and this cap. Where the table maps P0 to `advisory`, a cap of `acknowledge` changes nothing.
- The key merges upward as every other setting does: key by key, nearest file first. It is not part of the walk. A file that writes only `preExisting` has not spoken about any finding, and a file that speaks about a finding does not erase a farther file's cap. The maintainer confirmed this.
- A member of "Pre-existing, important" also has a floor of `advisory`, which [Trust](#trust) lists.

A pre-existing finding never resolves `block`. By default it is advisory. A folder may cap a severity at `acknowledge`.
It then takes the repository-wide acknowledgement gate above, with no separate gate for pre-existing findings.

It applies that filter to every counted round, including the round of exactly merge-base..H. The filter is there to drop a wider, older-base round's findings in files the merge no longer touches. But a pre-existing finding has no trigger, since a trigger names the hunk that caused it. So every pre-existing finding in a file the change did not touch is dropped from the exact round too. Under a `resolution.preExisting` cap of `acknowledge`, such a finding resolves acknowledge. The acknowledge-status rule says it "then takes the repository-wide acknowledgement gate", and rule 9 says "An unresolved acknowledge finding fails the gate".
explanation.whatToDo: Apply the path filter only to rounds whose revision is not the merge's own, or only to findings whose cause is introduced or affected. Keep every finding of a round of exactly merge-base..H, and keep pre-existing findings that resolve acknowledge. Add a test with a `preExisting: { P1: acknowledge }` policy and a lens finding in a file off the diff.
explanation.whyHere: The change grants an exemption to a class of finding, those off the merge's diff, that was meant only for older-base rounds' stale findings. That exemption opens a fail-closed rule: an acknowledgement the round's own verdict holds unresolved, and which fails that round's status, disappears from the gate. The gate then lets the head merge with nobody having answered it.

properties.failureScenario:
The base tip's root `melian.yaml` sets `resolution.preExisting.P1: acknowledge`, a documented opt-in. Pull request #N changes `src/a.ts` only. The round of exactly merge-base..H has a lens report a P1 in `src/caller.ts`, which the diff does not touch, and no evidence places its cause on the diff. Its cause is `pre-existing`, it has no trigger, and the round's adjudication resolves it `acknowledge`, so the round's own verdict is `findings` and does not pass.

In `RecordGate.#merged`, `proves(finding)` checks `[path]` = `["src/caller.ts"]` against `revision.paths()` = `["src/a.ts"]` and returns false, so the finding never enters `live`. `findings.acknowledge` is empty, `passes()` returns true, and `melian gate "#N"` exits 0 with the acknowledgement unanswered. Under rule 9 the gate fails on that unresolved acknowledgement.
